title: Basic Newborn Care: Bath Time
objectives: Know when sponge baths are needed instead of tub baths
Prepare a bath that is safe for a newborn
Hold and watch baby safely during the bath
steps: Until the umbilical cord stump falls off, give sponge baths only. This usually happens by about one or two weeks of age.
Baby does not need a bath every day. Three baths a week during the first year may be enough.
For a tub bath, fill the basin with 2 inches of water that feels warm, not hot, on the inside of your wrist or elbow.
Use one hand to support baby's head and the other to guide baby into the water, feet first.
Never leave a baby alone in the bath, even for an instant.
disclaimer: Based on AAP guidance (HealthyChildren.org). Not medical advice.

questions.prompt: Baby is five days old and the umbilical cord stump is still attached. What kind of bath should you give?
options: A tub bath with 2 inches of water
A quick shower held in your arms
A long soak in the big bathtub
questions.explanation: Newborns get sponge baths only until the stump of the umbilical cord falls off.

questions.prompt: How often does a baby need a bath during the first year?
options: About three times a week may be enough
questions.explanation: Babies do not need a bath every day. Three baths per week during the first year may be enough.

questions.prompt: How do you check the water before a tub bath?
options: It should feel hot to your fingertips
Any temperature is fine if the bath is short
It should feel warm, not hot, on the inside of your wrist or elbow
questions.explanation: Fill the basin with 2 inches of water that feels warm, not hot, to the inside of your wrist or elbow.

questions.prompt: Baby is in the bath and you realize the towel is in another room. What do you do?
options: Step out quickly; a few seconds is fine
Take baby with you; never leave a baby alone in the bath
Ask baby's older sibling to watch for a minute
Leave baby in the water and call for someone from the door
questions.explanation: Never leave a baby alone in the bath, even for an instant.
